title: Cradle cap — flaky scalp in babies
summary: Yellowish scales on the scalp are common and usually harmless.
whatsNormal:
Cradle cap (seborrheic dermatitis) looks like greasy yellow or white flakes on the scalp.

• Common in the first weeks to months
• Not itchy for most babies and not contagious
• May also appear on eyebrows or behind ears
• Often clears on its own over weeks to months

Gentle care: soft brush, occasional baby shampoo, and a little oil before shampoo to loosen scales — never pick hard at scales.
watchFor: Spreading redness or oozing on the scalp
Rash spreading to face, neck folds, or diaper area with heavy redness
Baby seems uncomfortable when you touch the scalp
callDoctorIf: No improvement after several weeks of gentle home care and you want guidance
You are unsure if this is cradle cap or something else
